description: We are a team of curious and enthusiastic space explorers passionate about technology, innovation, and space science. As aspiring innovators, we aim to use creativity and AI-powered tools to transform complex space information into engaging and interactive experiences. Through this challenge, we hope to bring NASA's forgotten space equipment and missions back into the spotlight, helping people discover the stories, science, and achievements behind humanity's exploration of the Moon and Mars.
summary: Coopers Station | Cosmic Archive is an interactive 3D planetary archaeology web application that transforms silent, decommissioned NASA spacecraft across the Moon, Mars, and deep space into living educational stories for school-aged explorers and space enthusiasts. Rather than burying mission history inside static spreadsheets or dense academic papers, our platform lets users orbit photorealistic 3D globes, click real landing site coordinates, and inspect 18 iconic off-world artifacts—from the Apollo 11 Laser Ranging Retroreflector to Mars's Opportunity Rover, Ingenuity Helicopter, and deep-space sentinels like NEAR Shoemaker and Kepler. Each artifact pairs verified NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) telemetry with kid-friendly storytelling, audio narration, and an interactive, randomized Junior Archaeologist Quiz. By turning decommissioned hardware into an accessible, login-free digital museum, Coopers Station preserves humanity's off-world engineering heritage and inspires the next generation of explorers to understand how past robotic pioneers paved the way for future lunar and Martian missions.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Coopers Station | Cosmic Archive organizes off-world human heritage into three interactive 3D exploration wings plus an educational assessment and telemetry hub:

3D Solar System & Orbital Approach: Visitors launch from an interactive WebGL Solar System featuring dynamic solar terminator lighting and smooth orbital approach transitions into each destination.

Moon Explorer (6 Relics), Mars Outposts (8 Pins) & Deep Space (4 Sentinels): Users rotate and zoom into 3D planetary globes mapped with real landing coordinates (Apollo 11, Surveyor 3, Opportunity, Viking 1 & 2, InSight, Ingenuity, Dawn, Kepler, and more). Clicking any pin opens a Story Drawer with mission timelines, scientific discoveries, "Why It Was Left Behind" explanations, and built-in voice narration.

Telemetry & Survival Analytics: Visualizes planned lifespans versus actual survival multipliers (such as Opportunity's 56.7x endurance record) alongside direct archival citations to NASA PDS, LROC, the Mars Exploration Program, and the Apollo Lunar Surface Journal (ALSJ).

Randomized Junior Archaeologist Quiz: Draws 5 randomized questions with shuffled answer options from a 12-question pool spanning the Moon, Mars, and deep space, awarding an Explorer Rank score card upon completion.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Designed for both young learners and space enthusiasts, the app removes barriers to STEM engagement by requiring zero logins, accounts, or high-end hardware. Teachers, students, and families can open the live web link on any laptop or mobile browser to explore real NASA coordinates and engineering milestones interactively.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

Frontend & 3D Rendering: React 18, Vite, JavaScript (ES6+), Three.js (WebGL with ACES Filmic tone mapping), and Tailwind CSS.

Data & Assets: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS), Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) elevation/albedo maps, NASA Mars Exploration Program archives, and Apollo Lunar Surface Journal records.

Development & Deployment: Built by Team Coopers Station using Visual Studio Code and Google Antigravity, version-controlled on GitHub (atheeqhussain22-oss/coopers-station-cosmic-archive), and deployed continuously via Netlify.
